newsitem.title: USA: Digital Q3 better-than-expected, stock up.
newsitem.headline: Digital Q3 better-than-expected, stock up.

text.p: Digital Equipment Corp reported a better-than-expected third quarter, even amid a tax rate that was higher than some analysts were forecasting, and its shares are expected to gain, traders and analysts said.

"It was a better-than-expected quarter," said John Jones, a Salomon Brothers analyst. "Revenue was in line with our expectations." He added that Digital's tax rate was higher than he had been forecasting for the quarter.
Digital reported third quarter earnings of $0.27 a share, compared with a First Call consensus estimate of $0.24.
Digital's shares were up in pre-opening trading.
"It was a very nice number," said one technology trader, adding that the company's cash balance was quite impressive.
Jones said that if Digital had been using his lower tax rate, earnings would have been even better than reported. "It would have been closer to $0.35 (a share)," Jones said.

But analysts were also concerned about Digital's lack of comments on its product line designed around its Alpha processors. Gary Helmig, of SoundView Financial said Alpha sales had been growing at 30 to 40 percent.
"The fact that they didn't comment on Alpha means that Alpha probably wasn't very good," Jones said.
